doc.subscription_method:
Bank financed subscription: The maximum multiple of the broker's bank financing ("up to 10x leverage") varies by stock. Some popular stocks have quota limits, and some stocks do not support this bank financing method.
Regular subscription: You can use the withdrawable HKD in your account for cash subscription, or use your account assets (including stock market value as collateral, available HKD cash, and cash in other currencies converted at the exchange rate) for IPO subscription with currency borrowing.
doc.buying_power:
Taking HKD as an example (the same rules apply to other currencies), the broker supports using available cash and stock collateral in your account as principal for IPO subscription.
Principal available for IPO subscription is defined as: the market value of held stocks converted at a certain margin ratio + the available cash in the account.
Broker financed IPO subscription means borrowing currency against pledged stocks, and automatically converting cash in currencies other than HKD into HKD for IPO subscription. If the withdrawable HKD is insufficient when the payment is deducted at the end of the subscription, broker financing is used by default and "financing interest" is charged.
Note: Cash accounts do not have the broker financing service, so the IPO buying power of a cash account does not include broker financing. The broker financing portion can be repaid at any time through a deposit or currency exchange.
doc.financing_interest:
Taking HKD as an example (the same rules apply to other currencies).
For margin accounts, daily IPO subscription financing interest = IPO subscription bank financing interest + IPO subscription broker financing interest = IPO subscription bank financing amount * bank financing interest rate / 365 + HKD broker financing amount * broker financing interest rate / 365.
Note: Cash accounts do not have the broker financing service, so the IPO subscription financing interest calculation does not include a broker financing interest portion.
IPO subscription bank financing interest rate: Refer to the subscription page; it varies by stock.
Broker financing interest rate: Check it under "Assets - My Rates".
Daily financing interest is for reference only; the statement prevails.
doc.cut_off_time:
Cash and broker financed subscription: The deadline is 09:00 on the date announced by the exchange.
"Up to 10x" bank financed subscription: Because the subscription procedures need to be processed, the subscription period ends 1 business day before the date announced by the exchange, usually at 16:00. Refer to the subscription page for details.
To make sure your IPO subscription succeeds, deposit funds in advance.
doc.financing_estimate:
If the withdrawable amount in the corresponding currency of the account is insufficient when the payment is deducted at the end of the subscription, broker financing is used by default. The value here is an estimate; "financing interest" is charged based on the actual funds in the account on each trading day after the deduction.

doc.notice:
1. The subscription amount is frozen in real time after the application is submitted and is deducted on the deadline date (the exact time is subject to the order status change). Subscription orders can only be canceled before the deadline. Regular subscription closes at 09:00 on the deadline date. Because the subscription procedures need to be processed, bank financed subscription ends 1 business day before the date announced by the exchange, usually at 16:00. Refer to the financed subscription page for details.

2. When a regular subscription amount exceeds the value of your HKD cash, currency borrowing financing is incurred, which in turn incurs interest. Keep an eye on your account assets.

3. IPOs are subject to the risk of delayed or canceled listing. In the event of a delay or cancellation, financing interest and subscription handling fees already charged are not refunded.

4. After the allotment results are announced, allotment information is updated in the subscription records or pushed as an in-app message. If you use financed subscription, keep an eye on your account funds. If the account margin is insufficient on the first day of listing, the allotted IPO shares may be force-liquidated.

5. For other questions about IPO subscription, see the Securities IPO Subscription Statement and IPO Subscription FAQ, or contact customer service.
